domain_restrictions: f is a total function from the Euclidean plane R^2 to the two-element set {red,green}
A,B,C,P,O are points of the Euclidean plane R^2
the hypothesis applies only to triples A,B,C that are noncollinear (hence distinct) so the circumcenter is uniquely defined in R^2
the circumcenter operation circ(A,B,C) is the unique intersection of perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC (uses Euclidean geometry)
root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every function f: R^2 -> {red,green}, if for all points A,B,C in R^2 that are noncollinear and satisfy f(A)=f(B)=f(C) we have f(circumcenter(A,B,C)) = f(A), then there exists a color c in {red,green} such that for every point P in R^2, f(P)=c. Equivalently: ∀f [(∀A,B,C (noncollinear ∧ f(A)=f(B)=f(C) ⇒ f(circumcenter(A,B,C))=f(A))) ⇒ (∃c ∈ {red,green} ∀P f(P)=c)].
quantifier_order: forall f : R^2 -> {red,green} (consider any 2-coloring of the plane)
assume (hypothesis) forall A,B,C in R^2: if A,B,C are noncollinear and f(A)=f(B)=f(C) then f(circumcenter(A,B,C)) = f(A)
conclude: exists c in {red,green} such that forall P in R^2, f(P) = c

payload.theorem_nl: Suppose that each point in the plane is colored either red or green, subject to the following condition: For every three noncollinear points $A,B,C$ of the same color, the center of the circle passing through $A,B$ and $C$ is also this color. Prove that all points of the plane are the same color.

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Assume a coloring f satisfies the circumcenter condition. Suppose, toward a contradiction, that both colors occur; choose O red and G green. Let r=|OG| and rho=r/3. By the circle bound around a green center, the small circle circle(G,rho) contains five distinct green points X1,...,X5. For each Xi, the geometric support construction produces two points on the fixed large circle circle(O,r) whose circumcenter with O is Xi; since O is red and Xi is green, not both support points can be red, so Xi has at least one green support point Ai on circle(O,r) with |XiAi|=|XiO|. The incidence bound says one fixed support point A on circle(O,r) can serve at most two Xi, so five distinct Xi force at least three distinct green support points A1,...,A5 on circle(O,r). But a circle centered at a red point O cannot contain three green points, because those three points would have circumcenter O and hence force O to be green. Contradiction. Therefore the coloring is constant. Choosing c as the color of the origin yields the exact existential conclusion.

steps.derives: Fix an arbitrary coloring f : R^2 -> {red,green} satisfying the hypothesis that every noncollinear monochromatic triple has a circumcenter of the same color. To prove the theorem, it is enough to show that all points of R^2 have one common color.
steps.trivial_justification: This sets up the implication in the root theorem: we take an arbitrary f under the stated hypothesis and aim to construct a color c with f(P)=c for all P.

steps.derives: Assume for contradiction that not all points of R^2 have the same color. Then there exist points O,G in R^2 such that f(O)=red and f(G)=green.
steps.trivial_justification: If the coloring is not constant and the codomain is exactly {red,green}, then both colors occur somewhere. Choose O of color red and G of color green.

steps.derives: Let r = dist(O,G). Then r>0 because O and G have different colors and therefore O != G. Define rho = r/3. Then 0<rho<r/2.
steps.trivial_justification: Different colors imply O != G, so the Euclidean distance r is positive. From rho=r/3 one gets rho>0 and rho<r/2 by arithmetic.

steps.derives: There exist five pairwise distinct points X1,X2,X3,X4,X5 on circle(G,rho) such that f(Xi)=green for each i=1,2,3,4,5.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L2 to the green center G and the positive radius rho.

steps.derives: For each i in {1,2,3,4,5}, there exists a point Ai on circle(O,r) such that f(Ai)=green and dist(Xi,Ai)=dist(Xi,O). Choose one such Ai for each i.
steps.trivial_justification: Each Xi is green and lies on circle(G,rho), while O is red and G is green, so L7 applies separately to X1,...,X5 and produces green support points A1,...,A5 on circle(O,r).

steps.derives: At least three of the points A1,A2,A3,A4,A5 are distinct. Therefore circle(O,r) contains three distinct green points.
steps.trivial_justification: The hypotheses of L8 are satisfied: rho<r/2 by A3, the Xi are pairwise distinct by A4, and each Ai lies on circle(O,r) with dist(Xi,Ai)=dist(Xi,O) by A5. L8 yields that at least three Ai are distinct; since each Ai is green by A5, these are three distinct green points on circle(O,r).

steps.derives: Contradiction: circle(O,r) cannot contain three distinct green points because f(O)=red.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L1 with the red center O and radius r. L1 says there are at most two green points on circle(O,r), contradicting A6.

steps.derives: Hence the assumption in A2 was false. Therefore all points of R^2 have the same color.
steps.trivial_justification: This is the direct negation of the contradiction assumption in A2.

steps.derives: Let P0 be the origin (0,0) in R^2 and set c = f(P0). Then c belongs to {red,green}, and by A8 one has f(P)=c for every point P in R^2. Therefore there exists c in {red,green} such that for every P in R^2, f(P)=c.
steps.trivial_justification: A8 states that every two points have the same color. Evaluating at the specific point P0=(0,0) gives a witness color c=f(P0), and then every P has color c.

steps.derives: For every function f : R^2 -> {red,green}, if for all noncollinear points A,B,C of R^2 with f(A)=f(B)=f(C) we have f(circumcenter(A,B,C))=f(A), then there exists a color c in {red,green} such that for every point P in R^2, f(P)=c.
steps.trivial_justification: A1 fixed an arbitrary f under the root hypothesis, and A9 derived exactly the required conclusion for that arbitrary f.

candidates.strategy_summary: Use a local contradiction built from two opposite-colored points O and G, a small circle around G, and a fixed circle around O. This explicitly fixes the earlier failures by avoiding any false global classification of circumcenter-closed subsets such as 'noncollinear implies the whole plane'; every key lemma uses hypotheses genuinely available from the 2-coloring setup. It also repairs the previously noted circle-interface issue by using the correct bridge: support points are taken from the intersection of circle(O, |OG|) and circle(X, |OX|), not from an equal-radius special case.
